artworks.title: Myrrha and Cinyras
artworks.description: Zanchi's Warsaw canvas stages Ovid's Cypriot horror: Cinyras and his daughter Myrrha — the king-priest of Aphrodite caught in the incest that will birth Adonis from the myrrh-tree.

artworks.title: Myrrha and Cinyras
artworks.description: Solis' Metamorphoses woodcut reduces the Cypriot scandal to a print: Cinyras and Myrrha as a standard Ovid plate — the father whose unknowing crime seeds Adonis' birth.

artworks.title: Cinyras Tries to Kill His Daughter Myrrha
artworks.description: A Rijksmuseum theatrical print shows Cinyras turning on Myrrha once he knows — the Cypriot king between Aphrodite's cult, incestuous darkness, and the chase that ends in her arboreal metamorphosis.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Ovid's Cinyras is the Paphian king undone by Myrrha's passion — the father of Adonis through a crime he discovers too late.

popCulture.title: Cinyras
popCulture.description: Legendary king and priest of Aphrodite at Paphos — father of Myrrha and, through her, of Adonis.
